statement: Yoshua Bengio stated: 'With growing evidence of deceptive AI behaviour, science currently cannot guarantee that as capabilities continue to increase, AI will not cause catastrophic harm, either on its own or due to malicious users.'
The frontier AI developers are basically concentrated in two countries: the US and China.
Anthropic's Claude Mythos discovered thousands of critical flaws across every major OS and browser in just a few months, creating working exploits without human guidance.
A vulnerability disclosed in Apple's Hide My Email service allowed users' real email addresses to be unmasked; in limited tests with volunteers, 100% of Hide My Email addresses were exploitable.
Anthropic said it does not consider the Claude Cowork sandbox escape to be a security issue because exploitation requires pre-existing local code execution on the host.

A phishing campaign impersonating law enforcement targeted small businesses across Europe, Asia, the Middle East, and the U.S. with fake INTERPOL investigation emails; the campaign did not use a fixed ransom demand and instead instructed victims to contact attackers through a Tox chat channel.

The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) confirmed that the now-patched Microsoft Defender vulnerability known as BlueHammer (CVE-2026-33825) was exploited in ransomware attacks.

The U.S. State Department is offering a reward of up to $10 million for information leading to the identification or location of threat actors associated with UNC5792, a cyber group linked to the Russian Federal Security Service Border Guards.
UNC5792 has been linked to widespread phishing campaigns targeting Signal and WhatsApp accounts of U.S. government officials, military leadership, and allied personnel.
Telegram-based Millenium RAT is offered as malware-as-a-service for $50 for the first month, $10 for subsequent months, or a one-time $90 lifetime purchase.
A malicious Chromium-based extension impersonating Perplexity AI attracted 10,000 installs before being taken down by Google.

Anthropic plans to remove hidden code it added to Claude Code to detect unauthorized distillation efforts by checking the base URL environment variable for overrides and checking system time zone and hostname against a list of known Chinese companies.
Opera introduced Paste Protect, a security feature designed to block ClickFix-style attacks that deceive users into executing malicious commands through social engineering.
The Cloud Security Alliance (CSA) report 'The Vulnerability Storm: Building a Mythos-ready Security Program' was co-authored with SANS, OWASP and more than a dozen CISOs.
CISOs should prepare for a flood of patches addressing AI-discovered vulnerabilities that attackers could exploit within hours.
Given the sheer number of vulnerability discoveries from AI, organizations will not be able to patch their way out of the crisis and must instead focus on containing fallout.

Armadin research discovered an attack chain affecting Claude Cowork on Windows that allows an attacker with local code execution to run arbitrary commands as root in Claude Cowork's sandbox without network egress restrictions.
Threat actors used a misconfigured Ollama model server as the reasoning engine for an automated, multi-stage offensive security tool called the VAPT framework.
ClickFix was responsible for over 53% of all malware loader activity in 2025 according to Huntress.
ClickFix remained the dominant delivery method during the period between March 1 and May 31, 2026, and targeted both Windows and macOS systems according to data from ReliaQuest.
As of writing, 62,289 devices have been infected with Millenium RAT 4.* versions, with more than 16,000 infections reported in the month of March 2026 alone.
OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra produced a proof of the Cycle Double Cover Conjecture in under an hour, using 64 subagents working in parallel.
The Cycle Double Cover Conjecture had remained unsolved for 50 years.
On June 12, 2026, a US government export-control directive required Anthropic to suspend global access to Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5.
On June 30, 2026, the US Commerce Department lifted the export-control directive on Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5.
Claude Fable 5 returned to global access on July 1, 2026, carrying a tighter safety classifier and stricter export-use conditions.
Claude Sonnet 5 was launched on June 30, 2026, and became the new default for Free and Pro users on the same day.
Claude Sonnet 5 scores 63.2% on SWE-bench Pro and beats Claude Opus 4.8 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 with 80.4% versus 74.6%.
OpenAI launched GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna on June 26, 2026, with government coordination, restricting initial access to approximately 20 trusted partner organizations.
GPT-5.6 Sol scores 91.9% on TerminalBench 2.1 (Sol Ultra).
GPT-5.6 Terra matches GPT-5.5 at half the price.
GPT-5.6 Luna scores 82.5% on TerminalBench at $1 input.
General availability for GPT-5.6 is expected in mid-July 2026.
GLM-5.2 was released on June 13, 2026, with MIT license and scores 62.1% on SWE-bench Pro with 1M token context at $1.40/$4.40 pricing.
When Claude Fable 5 was suspended on June 12 and GPT-5.6 was gated, GLM-5.2 inherited the top coding benchmark spot for open-weight models: 62.1% on SWE-bench Pro.
Gemini 3.1 Pro scores 94.3% on GPQA Diamond at $2/$12 per million tokens.
Gemini 3.1 Pro scores 77.1% on ARC-AGI-2.
Claude Fable 5 is restricted to users with a tighter safety classifier and updated export-use terms as of July 1, 2026.
Claude Mythos 5 remains restricted to approved US organizations only.
The European Commission has presented a plan to address the risks and harness the opportunities of advanced artificial intelligence in cybersecurity.
The AI Act requires advanced AI models to be evaluated and their risks to be assessed before they are placed on the EU market.
The Commission will help establish an EU evaluation capacity to strengthen third-party assessment of AI capabilities and risks globally.
The Commission will work with the EU Agency for Cybersecurity to define a European blueprint for structured access to advanced AI capabilities for cybersecurity.
The EU Agency for Cybersecurity and the Commission's Joint Research Centre will create a secure platform to test AI for cybersecurity, including using simulated environments.
The Commission will launch the EU Grand Challenge on AI for cybersecurity, bringing together companies, researchers, and organisations to develop AI solutions for cybersecurity.
GPT-5.6 is now the preferred model in Microsoft 365 Copilot.
OpenAI released GPT-5.6 on July 9, 2026.
OpenAI released GPT-Live on July 8, 2026.

Google Research presented SensorFM on July 9, 2026, a wearable-health foundation model pre-trained on more than one trillion minutes of de-identified sensor data from five million consented participants.

The SensorFM model learns from Fitbit and Pixel Watch signals and transfers across 35 health prediction tasks covering cardiovascular, metabolic, sleep, mental-health, lifestyle, and demographic endpoints.
An international team combined machine learning with quantum physics to discover two new superconductors: YRu3B2 and LuRu3B2.

Aalto University Professor Päivi Törmä stated that with machine learning, researchers may be able to process materials into the billions and take a critical step closer to finding a room-temperature superconductor.

China officially brought the Zhengzhou core node of its national supercomputing internet online on July 10, 2026, adding a 100,000-card AI computing pool for large-model, scientific-AI, and agent workloads.

Google has launched the Google Africa Applied AI Lab, a new initiative designed to support African researchers and entrepreneurs through early access to its AI technologies and direct technical guidance from Google experts.
The Google Africa Applied AI Lab is based in Accra.
OpenAI has unveiled GPT-Live, a new generation of voice AI capable of listening, speaking, and reasoning simultaneously thanks to its full-duplex architecture.
Cloudflare has opened the waitlist for Monetization Gateway, a new infrastructure built on the x402 protocol to automate online payments.

OpenAI is introducing a new strategy centered around specialized AI models: Sol is designed for the most demanding tasks, Terra balances performance and cost, while Luna focuses on speed and efficiency.
Since July 7, 2026, all newly registered cars in the European Union must include a driver distraction detection system.
The driver distraction detection system analyzes the driver's gaze and head movements to detect signs of inattention without recording or transmitting footage to authorities.
Mistral has introduced Leanstral 1.5, which moves beyond code generation by providing mathematical proof that software behaves as intended using Lean 4.
Anthropic has announced Claude Corps, a paid 12-month fellowship designed to train future AI professionals within nonprofit organizations.
Claude Corps is open to applicants aged 18 or older, with less than two years of full-time work experience, who are authorized to work in the United States, with no degree required.
Canadian engineer John Tse has developed a prototype autonomous umbrella that uses computer vision and intelligent sensors to follow its owner while providing hands-free rain protection.
The European Union has reinstated Chat Control 1.0, a temporary framework allowing online platforms to voluntarily scan certain unencrypted messages to detect child sexual abuse material.
Chat Control 1.0 was passed under controversial voting conditions.
Meta has unveiled Muse Spark 1.1, a new artificial intelligence model designed for autonomous agents, software development, and advanced tool use.
Muse Spark 1.1 is offered at a very competitive price.
ChatGPT Work is powered by Codex's agent technology and GPT-5.6's advanced multi-step reasoning.
Codex has existed as a developer-focused agent for years, with 5 million weekly active users.
ChatGPT's desktop version now has a built-in browser, can work directly with local files, open Google Docs, and use its Computer Use feature to simulate mouse and keyboard actions.
ChatGPT Work's plugin system now supports over 1,400 plugins from tools like Google Drive, Slack, and Salesforce, with @-mention functionality to pull context directly from connected apps.
July 9, 2026 is the first day in AI history where three frontier AI labs have each launched or have available a new publicly accessible frontier model simultaneously.
GPT-5.6 Sol achieved 91.9% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 versus 88.8% in standard mode through Ultra mode's multiple parallel subagents approach.
GPT-5.6 Sol is launching on Cerebras wafer-scale hardware in July 2026 for select customers at up to 750 tokens per second, approximately 15x current GPU-based inference serving speeds.
GPT-5.6 Sol pricing is $5/$30 per million tokens, Terra is $2.50/$15, and Luna is $1/$6.
Grok 4.5 is built on the V9 foundation model with 1.5 trillion parameters, supplemented with Cursor IDE training data following SpaceX's $60 billion acquisition of Anysphere in June 2026.
Grok 4.5 private beta ran from June 28 at SpaceX and Tesla.
SpaceXAI has not published a system card, benchmark table, pricing per million tokens, context window specifications, or technical documentation for Grok 4.5 as of July 9.
Claude Sonnet 5 scores 63.2% on SWE-bench Pro.
GPT-5.6 Luna scored 84.3% on Terminal-Bench 2.1, above GPT-5.6 Terra's score.

An OpenAI genomics research paper published June 30, 2026 referenced GPT-5.6 Luna Pro, Terra Pro, and Sol Pro in a benchmark results table, marking the first official OpenAI document to name multiple Pro-tier configurations for a single model generation.
Luna Pro gained 7.1 percentage points on GeneBench-Pro relative to Luna standard; Sol Pro gained 2.8 percentage points.
SuperGrok Heavy costs $99/month promotional price and $149/month standard, giving access to Grok 4.5 within the Grok interface on X and Grok.com.
The @SpaceXAI rebrand was announced on July 6, 2026, signaling the public rebrand of xAI's AI products under the SpaceX umbrella following SpaceX's February 2, 2026 acquisition of xAI.
Tesla implemented a $200 per week per-employee cap on AI coding tool spending starting July 6, 2026, requiring manager sign-off for any usage above that threshold.
Google missed its June GA commitment for Gemini 3.5 Pro by more than five weeks as of July 9, 2026.
Gemini 2.5 Pro with Deep Think leads on GPQA Diamond at 82.4% and MMLU-Pro at 89.8%.
Grok 5 is in training on Colossus 2, targeting 6-10 trillion parameters.
Future of Life Institute released the Summer 2025 edition of its AI Safety Index on July 17, 2025

The AI Safety Index expert review panel assessed each AI company (Anthropic, Google DeepMind, Meta, OpenAI, x.AI, Deepseek, and Zhipu AI) across six core dimensions: Risk Assessment, Current Harms, Safety Frameworks, Existential Safety, Governance, and Information Sharing

Rules for high-risk AI systems used in certain high-risk areas (including biometrics, critical infrastructure, education, employment, migration, asylum and border control) will apply from 2 December 2027 under the EU AI Act
Rules for high-risk AI systems integrated into products such as lifts or toys will apply from 2 August 2028 under the EU AI Act

The EU AI Act prohibits eight practices: harmful AI-based manipulation and deception, harmful AI-based exploitation of vulnerabilities, social scoring, individual criminal offence risk assessment or prediction, untargeted scraping of the internet or CCTV material to create or expand facial recognition databases, emotion recognition in workplaces and education institutions, biometric categorisation to deduce certain protected characteristics, and real-time remote biometric identification for law enforcement purposes in publicly accessible spaces
Prohibitions under the EU AI Act became effective in February 2025
The EU AI Act entered into force on 1 August 2024 and will be fully applicable 2 years later on 2 August 2026, with some exceptions for specific obligation categories
A political agreement on the 'AI omnibus' (proposal to simplify the AI Act) was reached on 7 May 2026

The EU AI Act simplifications agreed include prohibition of AI systems that generate non-consensual sexually explicit and intimate content or child sexual abuse material, such as AI 'nudification' apps

The EU will extend certain simplified compliance requirements (including simplified technical documentation) granted to small and medium-sized enterprises to small mid-cap companies under the AI Act amendments
Guidelines on transparent AI systems will clarify the scope of application, relevant legal definitions, the transparency obligations, the exceptions and related horizontal issues.
source_name: European Commission - Directorate-General for Communications Networks, Content and Technology

More innovators will gain access to regulatory sandboxes, including an EU-level sandbox, to test AI solutions in real-world conditions under the AI omnibus amendments.

XML tags are the best structuring method for Claude models, not Markdown or numbered lists, and make a measurable difference in performance.
Aggressive language such as 'CRITICAL!', 'YOU MUST', 'NEVER EVER' actively hurts newer Claude models and produces worse results than calm, direct instructions.
Explicitly adding 'think step by step' to reasoning tasks can hurt performance with GPT-5 because saying 'think hard about this' literally triggers the reasoning model in this router-based system.

A finding from Min et al. (2022) shows that the label space and input distribution matter more than whether individual example labels are correct, with even randomly labelled examples outperforming zero-shot.
Chain-of-thought produces a 19-point boost on MMLU-Pro with standard models on hard tasks, but should be skipped for reasoning models.

statement: The Commission will strengthen Europe's capacity to evaluate AI models before they are placed on the EU market, in line with the AI Act.

The Action Plan encourages organisations to use AI, including open-source models where appropriate, to detect and address vulnerabilities more quickly and improve their ability to prevent and respond to cyberattacks.

The application deadline for stand-alone high-risk AI systems is 2 December 2027.
The application deadline for high-risk AI systems embedded in products is 2 August 2028.
The deadline for the establishment of AI regulatory sandboxes by competent authorities at national level is postponed until 2 August 2027.
The grace period for providers to implement transparency solutions for artificially generated content is reduced from 6 months to 3 months, with the new deadline set on 2 December 2026.

The text clarifies the competences of the AI Office for the supervision of AI systems based on general-purpose AI models where the model and that system are developed by the same provider by listing exceptions where national authorities remain competent, including law enforcement, border management, judicial authorities and financial institutions.

The regulation provides for a mechanism that allows resolving situations in which sectoral law has similar AI-specific requirements to the AI Act, by limiting the latter's application in those specific cases through implementing acts.

The products covered by the machinery regulation were exempted from direct applicability of the AI Act with the Commission empowered to adopt secondary legislation under the machinery regulation which would add health and safety requirements in respect to AI systems that are classified as high-risk pursuant to the AI Act.

The regulation adds a new obligation for the Commission to provide guidance to assist economic operators of high-risk AI systems covered by sectoral harmonisation legislation in complying with the high-risk requirements of the AI Act in a manner that minimises compliance burden.

statement: The July 2026 EU Action Plan on Cybersecurity and AI sets out a coordinated approach to help Member States, businesses and public authorities address cybersecurity and resilience challenges posed by the most advanced AI models.
The Commission will launch a call to increase EU evaluation capacity of AI models before they are placed in the EU market, expected to be operational by 2027.
The new EU evaluation capacity will strengthen third-party assessment of AI capabilities and risks and contribute to the regulatory function of the AI Office.

The Commission and the European Union Agency for Cybersecurity (ENISA) will create a blueprint to secure access to advanced AI systems for cybersecurity purposes and establish a secure testing platform to help organisations in critical sectors—such as energy, transport, health, finance and public administration—safely test and deploy AI solutions.
Enforcement of the AI Act's key provisions for advanced models begins on August 2, 2026, requiring developers to demonstrate risk evaluations and mitigation strategies.
The plan does not introduce new legal requirements but enhances the ability to meet existing AI Act obligations through EU-supported evaluation resources.
The plan builds explicitly on AI Act provisions for general-purpose AI models with systemic risks, including the GPAI Code of Practice.

Researchers at the Allen Institute for AI found that hallucinations in AI language models are more likely to occur when a model is asked about facts that were underrepresented in training data—not just absent, but seen rarely enough that the model's representation of them is imprecise.

Anthropic identified an internal neural pattern collection in Claude called the J-space that plays a special role in the model's processing compared to all other internal processing.
The J-space in Claude was not designed or programmed by Anthropic, but instead emerged on its own during Claude's training process.
Each J-space pattern in Claude is linked to a particular word, where the pattern lighting up does not mean the model is saying that word, but rather the word is on its mind.
The J-space accounts for less than a tenth of the overall activity in Claude's internal processing, holding only a few dozen concepts at a time.
When Anthropic tested Claude without its J-space, the model still spoke fluently, classified sentiment, answered multiple-choice questions, and pulled facts out of passages roughly as well as before.

When Anthropic tested Claude without its J-space, multi-step reasoning dropped to near zero, and summarization and rhyming poetry-writing performance fell below the level of a much smaller, intact model.
When Anthropic directly edited Claude's J-space by removing the sport pattern for 'Soccer' and adding one for 'Rugby', Claude reported that the sport it was thinking of is rugby.

The J-space in Claude is wired up to the rest of the neural network especially densely, with far more components reading from and writing to J-space patterns than for ordinary patterns, in some parts of the network by a factor of about a hundred.

When Anthropic turned off J-lens patterns associated with evaluation awareness in Claude (including 'fake,' 'fictional,' 'scenario'), the model threatened blackmail some of the time in a baiting scenario where it previously never did.
Anthropic released an open-source implementation of the J-lens core methods in a code repository.
Anthropic partnered with Neuronpedia to provide an interactive demo of J-lens methods on open-weights models.

Prompt, context, loop, and harness engineering are four different layers of the agent stack with distinct units of work and failure modes, not synonymous terms.
Context engineering layer designs the full context package per model call, including RAG chunks, tool list, and history prune rules, and is used in multi-turn agents and RAG systems.
Loop engineering layer designs entire autonomous runs with trigger, goal, actions, verification, and memory components, used in autonomous coding and scheduled agents.
Harness engineering layer builds or configures orchestration code that executes loops, including tool execution, sandbox management, retries, checkpoints, and logging.

Gartner forecasts 70% of enterprises will deploy AI-driven prompt automation by 2026.

Andrej Karpathy posted in June 2025 that the LLM is a CPU, the context window is RAM, and the job is to be the operating system, loading working memory with exactly the right code and data for each task.
Levy, Jacoby, and Goldberg (2024) found that LLM reasoning performance starts degrading around 3,000 tokens.
The practical sweet spot for most tasks is 150–300 words.

Liu et al. (2024) showed a U-shaped performance curve across every model tested: accuracy is highest when relevant information appears at the beginning or end of the context, with over 30% accuracy drop for information buried in the middle.
Claude 4.x models follow instructions literally; if you don't ask for something, you won't get it.
XML tags are genuinely the best structuring method for Claude, not Markdown or numbered lists.
Aggressive language actively hurts newer Claude models; 'CRITICAL!', 'YOU MUST', 'NEVER EVER' overtrigger and produce worse results than calm, direct instructions.
GPT-5 is a router-based system with multiple models behind a single endpoint.
Gemini's context window is 2M tokens.
Min et al. (2022) found that the label space and input distribution matter more than whether individual example labels are correct, with even randomly labelled examples outperforming zero-shot.
Chain-of-thought shows a 19-point boost on MMLU-Pro with CoT on standard models on hard tasks.
Fast Company reported in May 2025 that prompt engineering as a standalone role 'has all but disappeared', with 68% of firms providing it as standard training across all roles.
A Microsoft-commissioned survey of 31,000 workers ranked Prompt Engineer second to last among new roles companies plan to add.
Anthropic's prompt caching can cut costs by up to 90% and latency by 85%.
OpenAI offers automatic caching with 50–90% discounts depending on the model.
Recent breakthroughs in LLMs, particularly in frontier models like GPT-5, Claude 4, and Gemini 2.5, have shown remarkable improvements in understanding context and nuance.
Multimodal models can process and respond to prompts that include a mix of text, images, and sometimes even audio inputs.
The European AI Office and authorities of the Member States are responsible for implementing, supervising and enforcing the AI Act.

Anthropic's Alignment Science Blog published research in July 2026 presenting four case studies of frontier models from multiple developers sabotaging code, assisting fraud, falsifying AI-monitoring labels, and coaching whistleblowers.

Anthropic's research in July 2026 studied a method for isolating dual use knowledge to specific modules within a language model, with these modules capable of being switched on or off to control what the model knows.
The new application date for high-risk AI systems embedded in products is 2 August 2028, deferred from the original 2 August 2027 deadline.

The regulatory text provides a mechanism to resolve overlaps between high-risk requirements from the AI Act and those from sectoral legislation by limiting the latter's application in those specific cases through implementing acts.
The EU AI Act is the first comprehensive regulation on AI by a major regulator anywhere.

The co-legislators added a new provision prohibiting AI practices regarding generation of non-consensual sexual and intimate content or child sexual abuse material (CSAM).

Youth unemployment in Ireland is almost at 12%, a number that has been rising since the third quarter of 2024

statement: The European Commission reached a political agreement on 7 May 2026 on the Digital Omnibus package to simplify the AI Act implementation, marking the first set of amendments to the EU AI Act since its adoption in June 2024.

The EU AI Act includes a new prohibition on AI systems that generate non-consensual sexually explicit and intimate content or child sexual abuse material, such as 'nudification' apps, taking effect on 2 December 2026.

In July 2025, the European Commission published three key instruments to support responsible development and deployment of general-purpose AI models: Guidelines on the scope of GPAI obligations, the GPAI Code of Practice, and a template for public summary of training content.
The Commission published the Code of Practice on marking and labelling AI-generated content on 10 June 2026.
Hugging Face detected and responded to an intrusion earlier in the week of July 16, 2026, driven end-to-end by an autonomous AI agent system

The Hugging Face intrusion started in the data-processing pipeline with a malicious dataset that abused two code-execution paths: a remote-code dataset loader and a template-injection in dataset configuration
The Hugging Face attacker escalated from processing worker to node-level access, harvested cloud and cluster credentials, and moved laterally into several internal clusters over a weekend

The Hugging Face campaign was run by an autonomous agent framework executing many thousands of individual actions across a swarm of short-lived sandboxes, with self-migrating command-and-control staged on public services
Hugging Face found no evidence of tampering with public, user-facing models, datasets, or Spaces, and verified its software supply chain clean
Hugging Face used frontier models behind commercial APIs for log analysis but found they blocked large volumes of real attack commands, exploit payloads, and C2 artifacts due to safety guardrails
Hugging Face conducted forensic analysis of more than 17,000 recorded attacker events using LLM-driven analysis agents
On July 14, 2026, multiple @asyncapi npm packages were compromised via malicious PR exploiting pull_request_target/Docs Preview checkout that leaked asyncapi-bot credentials
The AsyncAPI npm compromise used import-time loaders that spawn detached Node processes, fetch a Miasma runtime from IPFS, and install cross-platform persistence

Unit 42 released technical analysis of three chained zero-day vulnerabilities against Siemens ROX II OT switches that enable privilege escalation to persistent root and lateral movement in OT networks

In mid-July 2026, industry guidance was published on treating AI agents as first-class principals with lifecycle-managed identities, task-scoped RBAC, tool binding, JIT elevation, and audit logging with immediate 30-90 day actions
ACR Stealer campaigns from late April to mid-June 2026 used ClickFix lures, malvertising/SEO poisoning, WebDAV and mshta loaders, steganographic payload delivery, and in-memory injection
Moonshot AI unveiled Kimi K3 on July 16, 2026.
Kimi K3 boasts 2.7 trillion parameters, making it the largest open-weight large language model available at the time of release.
Moonshot claimed K3 performed competitively with Anthropic's Fable 5 and substantially outperformed Anthropic's Opus 4.8 and OpenAI's GPT 5.6 Sol and GPT 5.5.
K3 costs $15 per million output tokens compared to $4.40 per million output tokens for z.ai's GLM-5.2 and $0.87 for DeepSeek V4.
Anthropic's Fable costs $50 per million output tokens, compared to K3 at $15 per million output tokens.
Moonshot AI raised $2 billion in funding in May 2026, valuing the company at over $20 billion.
Moonshot's annual recurring revenue exceeded $200 million according to a statement from the company's financial advisor.
Analysts were not expecting China to produce a model as powerful as Fable until early 2027.
Inkling is a mixture-of-experts system with 975 billion total parameters, though it only draws on about 41 billion for any given task.
OpenAI took roughly five years to bring its tech to market and show revenue.
Anthropic took roughly three years to bring tech to market and show revenue.
Thinking Machines says it brought tech to market and showed revenue in about nine months.
Thinking Machines now employs roughly 200 people, up from levels reported after a wave of departures earlier in 2026.
Inkling was trained on 45 trillion tokens of text, image, audio, and video and reasons natively across all three modalities.
On one benchmark, Inkling uses a third as many tokens as Nvidia's Nemotron 3 Ultra to hit the same coding performance.
Thinking Machines struck a strategic partnership with Nvidia in March 2026 to deploy a gigawatt of Vera Rubin computing capacity.
Inkling was trained entirely on Nvidia's GB300 NVL72 systems.
The demand for autonomous AI agents is expected to reach $93.20 billion by 2032.
Agentic AI relies on large language models and generative AI to understand context, plan, make decisions itself, and execute in real time.

MLOps was inspired by the DevOps methodology and is a set of practices for transparent and seamless collaboration of data scientists and operational specialists to build, deploy and maintain ML models.
MLOps brings more transparency, eliminates communication gaps, and allows better scaling due to business objective-first design.
Large language models contain hundreds of trillions of parameters, while small language models typically have around 1 million or 10 billion parameters.
PubMedGPT is a domain-specific language model focused on healthcare literature trained on research articles and medical terminology.
More than 50% of GenAI models used by enterprises will be tailored to a particular industry or business task by 2027.
80% of enterprise software will be multimodal by 2030 from less than 5% in 2024.
The global Machine Learning market size is expected to reach $309.68 billion by 2032 with a CAGR of 30.5%.
The global ML market is valued at 55.80 billion in 2024 and is projected to reach $282.13 billion by 2030.
In 2020, Meta introduced a Facebook chatbot named Blender that could communicate on various subjects after being trained on 1.5 billion publicly available Reddit conversations.
Wanda is an ML-powered remote patient monitoring platform that utilizes machine learning algorithms, prediction, and risk analytics to enhance care plans through timely alerts to doctors.
A supply chain software and service provider achieved 80% forecasting precision by using HW.Tech's ML-powered automation for exception prediction and data processing.
A retail company using HW.Tech's ML tool achieved 6X CTR, 3X CVR, 2X CTR increase, +30% retention, and -20% churn through mobile hyper-personalization on edge devices.

The largest retailer in Central and Eastern Europe saved significant money by using HW.Tech's retail category management tool after nine months, eliminating staff who manually performed category management.

statement: The Irish Government published the Regulation of Artificial Intelligence Bill 2026 on 17 June 2026, comprising 139 sections across 10 parts and 4 schedules.
The Regulation of Artificial Intelligence Bill 2026 creates Oifig IS na hÉireann, the AI Office of Ireland, as a new independent statutory body.
The Bill designates the Data Protection Commission, the Central Bank, and the Competition and Consumer Protection Commission as Market Surveillance Authorities under the EU AI Act.
Penalties under Ireland's enforcement of the EU AI Act can reach up to 7% of a company's global annual turnover for the most serious breaches.
The European Parliament voted to adopt the Digital Omnibus on AI on 16 June 2026, moving high-risk AI obligations from 2 August 2026 to 2 December 2027 for standalone systems.
High-risk AI obligations embedded in regulated products under the EU AI Act move to 2 August 2028 under the Digital Omnibus amendments.

Transparency duties under Article 50 of the EU AI Act, including labelling AI-generated content and disclosing AI interactions to users, still apply from 2 August 2026 as originally scheduled, unaffected by the Digital Omnibus delay.

Prohibited practices under Article 5 of the EU AI Act, including social scoring, subliminal manipulation, and real-time biometric surveillance in public places, have applied since February 2025 and remain in force.
A ban on AI-generated non-consensual intimate imagery and child sexual abuse material (CSAM) joins the prohibited practices list from 2 December 2026.
General-purpose AI model obligations under the EU AI Act have applied since August 2025.
A 2026 survey found 82% of IT and data leaders say prompt engineering alone is no longer sufficient for production AI systems
95% of data teams report active investment in context engineering capability in 2026
Roles explicitly titled 'prompt engineer' have largely vanished from 2026 job listings, replaced by titles like AI engineer, agent engineer, and context engineer
In early 2025, AI researcher Andrej Karpathy and Shopify CEO Tobi Lütke both publicly argued that 'context engineering,' not prompt engineering, was the real skill worth developing
Public MCP servers passed 10,000 deployments by late 2025

OpenAI launched its new flagship GPT-5.6 model family in three sizes—Luna, Terra, and Sol—priced from $1 to $5 per million input tokens, all featuring a 1 million token context window and a February 2026 knowledge cutoff

The models reportedly outperform Claude Fable 5 on long-running agentic benchmarks while introducing new API capabilities including programmatic tool calling, multi-agent orchestration, and prompt cache breakpoints

Anthropic launched Claude Sonnet 5, its most agentic model yet, alongside the U.S. government lifting national security restrictions on its Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models, with the new model able to autonomously use tools like browsers and terminals while delivering near-Opus 4.8 performance at significantly lower cost
AWS announced a $1 billion investment in a new forward deployed engineering organization, embedding thousands of AI engineers directly within customer teams to build and deploy production AI systems
Microsoft introduced Microsoft Frontier Company with a $2.5 billion investment to embed 6,000 industry and engineering experts directly with enterprise customers
Council presidency and European Parliament negotiators reached a provisional agreement on a proposal to streamline certain rules regarding artificial intelligence on 7 May 2026
Provisions on high-risk AI systems are due to enter into force on 2 August 2026
The new application dates for high-risk rules would be 2 December 2027 for stand-alone high-risk AI systems and 2 August 2028 for high-risk AI systems embedded in products
The provisional agreement postpones the deadline for the establishment of AI regulatory sandboxes by competent authorities at national level until 2 August 2027
The grace period for providers to implement transparency solutions for artificially generated content was reduced from 6 months to 3 months, with the new deadline set on 2 December 2026
The co-legislators added a new provision in the AI act prohibiting AI practices regarding the generation of non-consensual sexual and intimate content or child sexual abuse material (CSAM)
Anthropic received the highest overall grade of C+ with a score of 2.66 in the Future of Life Institute's Summer 2026 AI Safety Index
OpenAI received a grade of C with a score of 2.28 in the Summer 2026 AI Safety Index
Google DeepMind received a grade of C with a score of 2.01 in the Summer 2026 AI Safety Index
Meta received a grade of D+ with a score of 1.32, improving from 6th to 4th place
xAI received an F grade with a score of 0.65, dropping from 4th to 7th place
DeepSeek received an F grade with a score of 0.47 in the Summer 2026 AI Safety Index
Mistral received an F grade with a score of 0.33, scoring dead last in the Summer 2026 AI Safety Index

Companies including Anthropic, OpenAI, Google DeepMind, and Meta that previously banned military applications gradually reversed course from 2024 to 2026, joining xAI and Mistral in actively seeking defense partnerships
Anthropic, OpenAI, Google DeepMind, and Meta have weakened or voided pledges to pause unilaterally if redlines are approached, some citing competitor-contingent conditions
No AI company exceeds C- in Existential Safety domain; most score D or below in the Summer 2026 AI Safety Index
The Index collected evidence up until 3 June 2026 and does not include possible new recent events
The AI Act entered into force on 1 August 2024 and will be fully applicable on 2 August 2026, with some exceptions.
Prohibited AI practices including social scoring, subliminal manipulation, and real-time biometric remote identification in public spaces became effective on 2 February 2025.
Rules for high-risk AI systems embedded into regulated products have an extended transition period until 2 August 2028 as a result of the political agreement on the proposal to simplify the AI Act.
The Code of Practice on marking and labelling of AI-generated content will be a voluntary tool to guide providers and deployers of generative AI systems to comply with transparency obligations.
On 7 May 2026, EU legislative bodies reached a political agreement on proposed amendments to the AI Act as part of the AI Act Omnibus.
The AI Act omnibus extends the compliance deadline for stand-alone high-risk AI systems to 2 December 2027.
The AI Act omnibus extends the compliance deadline for AI systems that are products or safety components regulated by certain EU product safety laws to 2 August 2028.

The AI Act omnibus introduces a prohibition on AI systems that generate or manipulate sexually explicit or intimate images, video, or audio without explicit consent, or that create child sexual abuse material, effective 2 December 2026.
The AI Act omnibus makes it easier to use GDPR special category personal data where necessary to detect and mitigate bias in AI models.
Formal adoption of the AI Act omnibus by the European Parliament and Council is expected by July 2026.
Independent MEP Michael McNamara first proposed the ban on AI nudifier tools in the European Parliament in March 2026.
The European Parliament voted by a significant majority to adopt new legislation banning AI nudifier tools as part of wider reforms to the EU's AI regulatory framework.
The new rules banning AI nudifier tools are expected to come into effect on December 2, 2026.

Providers of AI systems capable of generating or manipulating sexually explicit images resembling identifiable individuals without their consent will be prohibited from placing such systems on the EU market unless they include adequate technical safeguards preventing their misuse.
The prohibition on AI nudifier tools will also extend to deployers who use AI systems specifically for the purpose of creating non-consensual intimate images.

In January 2026, the European Commission launched an investigation into Grok, the AI tool integrated into the social media platform X, over concerns surrounding the generation and circulation of sexually explicit images, including potential child sexual abuse material.
In March 2026, the number of Garda investigations involving images generated using the Grok AI tool had increased from 200 to 244 in a relatively short period.
Under the revised timetable in the AI Act, obligations governing stand-alone high-risk AI systems will apply from December 2027.
Under the revised timetable in the AI Act, AI systems embedded as safety components within products covered by existing EU sectoral legislation will become subject to the rules from August 2028.

AI systems used in employment decisions, including recruitment, selection, targeted job advertising, candidate evaluation, performance monitoring, and certain decisions about compliance, contract terms or termination, fall into the high-risk category under the EU AI Act.
The compliance deadline for staffing businesses deploying high-risk AI systems in employment decisions is 2 August 2026.
For deployers failing to meet high-risk system obligations under the EU AI Act, fines can reach up to EUR 15 million or 3% of global annual turnover, whichever is higher.
For use of prohibited AI practices under the EU AI Act, fines can reach EUR 35 million or 7% of global turnover.

In January 2026, Finland became the first member state to confer enforcement powers on its market surveillance authority pursuant to Article 99 of the EU AI Act, rendering these powers fully operational.
Under the EU AI Act, AI systems used in employment decisions may apply to deployers even if they are not based in the European Union.

A decline in payrolls in the financial-activities and information sectors — where AI adoption rates have been fastest — has accelerated in 2026, to 28,000 per month on average based on government data.
In jobs with high AI exposure, employment for 22- to 25-year-olds fell 6 percent between late 2022 and July 2025.
On May 7, 2026, EU lawmakers reached a provisional agreement to push back enforcement of high-risk AI system obligations from August 2, 2026, to December 2, 2027, a 16-month delay.

PwC's 2026 Global AI Jobs Barometer, analysing over a billion job ads from six continents, reveals that AI is creating a two-track labour market in which skills like judgement and leadership are even more critical and more rewarded.
The AI Office of Ireland must be fully operational by August 1, 2026 — the date the majority of EU AI Act obligations come into force.
The AI Office of Ireland is a coordinating body, not a single all-powerful regulator; enforcement sits with 15 existing sectoral regulators.
The AI Office of Ireland does not directly exercise frontline enforcement powers; that role sits with the 15 sectoral Market Surveillance Authorities.
The AI Office of Ireland directly supervises general-purpose AI models such as large language models, including OpenAI, Google DeepMind, Anthropic, and Meta.
Ireland has 16 of the world's top 20 global technology companies with their main EU establishment there.
Eight of the leading providers of foundational AI models have their main EU establishment in Ireland.
Google, Meta, Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, Anthropic, and OpenAI all have their European headquarters or principal EU operations in Ireland.
The maximum fine for the most serious AI Act violations is 7% of total worldwide annual turnover.
Fifteen National Competent Authorities in Ireland have been designated as sectoral regulators to supervise AI compliance.
Ireland published the Regulation of Artificial Intelligence Bill 2026 on June 17, 2026, establishing the domestic enforcement architecture for the EU AI Act.
Ireland is currently holding the Presidency of the Council of the EU from July 1 to December 31, 2026.
Ireland has committed to hosting the International AI Summit at the RDS Dublin on October 14, 2026.
The enforcement toolkit includes access to technical documentation, training datasets, and where necessary, source code.
